headline: Q2FY27 Result Review

highlights: However, opex grew 27% and credit cost increased 72% YoY, moderating earnings growth.
BT-out declined 40bps YoY to 4%.  Earnings were held back by opex and credit cost: NII grew 27% YoY, supported by AUM growth and a 20bps improvement in spreads.
PAT growth excluding assignment income was 25% in Q2 and 28% in H1.

However, opex increased 27% YoY, faster than the 24% growth in net total income, while credit cost rose 72% YoY and 22% QoQ to Rs163mn, including a scheduled Rs60mn write-off.  Asset Quality: GNPA/NNPA remained stable QoQ at 1.5%/1.2%, while 30+ DPD was flat at 5.2%.

Management reiterated its target of 40-45 branch additions in FY27, mostly in H2, because the branches opened in H1FY26 have now matured enough to support the next round of expansion.  Disbursements through digital sourcing rose to 7% in Q2FY27 from 4% in Q2FY26, and management plans to scale this up significantly in coming quarters.
The company remains on track for its FY30 AUM target of Rs300bn.  Disbursements grew 21% YoY to Rs11.26bn, up 8% QoQ against comparable Q1 disbursements of Rs10.46bn on a clearance basis.
watch: Key Highlights and Investment Rationale  Disbursements recovered after the Q1 transition: Disbursements reached a record Rs11.3bn, averaging Rs3.75–3.8bn monthly, following the Q1 transition to cheque-realisation-based recognition.

Collection efficiency improved to 98% from 97% in Q1, and management expects legal recoveries to improve in H2.  Outlook: Management reiterated 25–30% guidance, expects 25–27% (GMA)%, disbursement growth of at least 20% and PAT growth of around 25%, assuming improved assignment volumes in H2.
